name: The Corner Office
subject: Business leaders and companies
tagline: Twenty questions on founders, deals and the companies that got big. Mixed formats. Starts easy, ends hard.

questions.q: Who co-founded Apple with Steve Wozniak in 1976?
questions.w: They started in the Jobs family garage in Los Altos. A third co-founder, Ronald Wayne, sold his ten percent stake within weeks for $800.

questions.q: Which company did Jeff Bezos start in 1994 as an online bookstore?
questions.w: It was briefly called Cadabra and run from a garage in Bellevue, Washington. He renamed it after the biggest river he could think of.

questions.q: Elon Musk founded Tesla.
questions.w: False. Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning founded Tesla in 2003. Musk led its first big funding round in 2004, became chairman, and took over as chief executive in 2008.

questions.q: Oprah Winfrey's production company is her first name spelled backwards. What is it called?
questions.w: Harpo Productions, founded in 1986, made her talk show. OWN, the Oprah Winfrey Network, came later in 2011.

questions.q: Warren Buffett built which Omaha company into one of the most valuable in the world?
questions.w: It began as a failing textile mill he bought in 1965. Its annual meeting is nicknamed Woodstock for Capitalists. In 2025 he announced Greg Abel would take over as chief executive.

questions.q: Ray Kroc turned McDonald's into a giant, but who opened the original restaurant?
questions.w: Richard and Maurice McDonald, in San Bernardino in 1940. Kroc joined as a franchise agent in 1954 and bought them out in 1961 for $2.7 million.

questions.q: Phil Knight started which company as Blue Ribbon Sports, selling Japanese running shoes from his car?
questions.w: He co-founded it with his old track coach, Bill Bowerman. A design student was paid $35 for the swoosh logo in 1971.

questions.q: Which of these companies famously started in a garage?
questions.w: Apple in Los Altos, Google in a Menlo Park garage rented from Susan Wojcicki, and Amazon in Bellevue. IBM began in 1911 as a merger of three established companies.

questions.q: Who founded Alibaba in 1999?
questions.w: A former English teacher, he started it in his Hangzhou apartment with seventeen friends. Pony Ma founded Tencent, Lei Jun founded Xiaomi and Robin Li founded Baidu.

questions.q: Indra Nooyi was chief executive of which company from 2006 to 2018?
questions.w: Born in Chennai, she pushed the company toward healthier products and was one of the few women running a Fortune 50 company at the time.

questions.q: Put these companies in order of founding, earliest first.
questions.w: Ford in 1903, IBM's predecessor in 1911 (renamed IBM in 1924), Microsoft in 1975 and Facebook in 2004.

questions.q: Reed Hastings co-founded which company in 1997, starting out by mailing DVDs?
questions.w: With Marc Randolph. In 2000 they offered to sell the company to Blockbuster for $50 million and were turned down.

questions.q: Coca-Cola was invented in 1886 by a man of which profession?
questions.w: John Pemberton, an Atlanta pharmacist, sold it as a tonic. Businessman Asa Candler bought the rights and built the company.

questions.q: Sara Blakely became a billionaire by founding which company?
questions.w: She started it in 2000 with $5,000 in savings and no outside investors. In 2021 she sold a majority stake at a $1.2 billion valuation.

questions.q: Long before phones, Nokia began in 1865 in which industry?
questions.w: It started as a wood-pulp mill in Finland. Rubber boots and cables came later, and mobile phones only in the 1980s.

questions.q: Which car company began as a maker of textile looms?
questions.w: Toyoda Automatic Loom Works. Kiichiro Toyoda set up the car division in 1933. Peugeot began with coffee mills and steel, Škoda with bicycles.

questions.q: Which of these does not belong to Google's parent company, Alphabet?
questions.w: WhatsApp has belonged to Meta since 2014. YouTube was bought in 2006, Waymo grew out of Google's self-driving project, and Fitbit was acquired in 2021.

questions.q: In 2014 Mary Barra became the first woman to run a major global carmaker. Which one?
questions.w: She joined GM at eighteen as a student inspecting fender panels and worked her way up over more than thirty years.

questions.q: In which year did Amazon buy Whole Foods?
questions.w: For $13.7 billion, its biggest purchase at the time. The company had gone public in 1997 and launched Prime in 2005.

questions.q: Which Indian group, founded in 1868, owns Jaguar Land Rover?
questions.w: Tata Motors bought Jaguar Land Rover from Ford in 2008 for $2.3 billion. The group was founded by Jamsetji Tata as a trading company.
